what_its_for: Flavoxate helps relieve uncomfortable bladder and urinary symptoms such as urgent need to urinate, needing to urinate frequently, pain or burning when you urinate, and bladder spasms. It works by relaxing the muscles in your bladder so you feel more comfortable.
how_to_take: Take flavoxate by mouth with a full glass of water. You can take it with or without food, but if it upsets your stomach, try taking it with food or milk. Swallow the tablet whole. Take it exactly as your doctor prescribed and do not take more than directed.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 100 mg to 200 mg taken 3 to 4 times a day. Your doctor will tell you the right dose for you. As your symptoms improve, your doctor may lower your dose. Do not change your dose on your own without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store flavoxate at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing any activity that requires clear vision or alertness until you know how this medicine affects you, because it can cause blurred vision, dizziness, or drowsiness. Avoid alcohol while taking flavoxate, as it can make drowsiness worse. Avoid becoming overheated or dehydrated, especially in hot weather or during exercise, since flavoxate can reduce sweating and raise your body temperature.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: difficulty urinating or no urination at all, fast or irregular heartbeat, severe confusion or hallucinations, high fever with hot and dry skin (signs of overheating), eye pain or vision changes, signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing. Also call your doctor if your bladder symptoms do not improve or if they get worse.
when_it_works: Many people start to notice some relief from their bladder symptoms within a few days of starting flavoxate. However, it may take up to 2 to 4 weeks to feel the full benefit. Keep taking it as prescribed even if you feel better, unless your doctor tells you to stop.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over) may be more sensitive to side effects like confusion, dizziness, and blurred vision, so extra caution is needed. Flavoxate is generally NOT recommended for children under 12 years of age. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before taking this medicine, as its safety has not been fully established. People with glaucoma, a blockage in the stomach or intestines, or trouble emptying their bladder should NOT take flavoxate — always tell your doctor your full medical history before starting this medication.
